title: OU 38, No. 1 Missouri 17: The 2007 Big 12 Championship Game
question: When did Oklahoma beat No. 1 Missouri in the Big 12 Championship Game?
answer: Oklahoma beat top-ranked Missouri 38-17 in the Big 12 Championship Game on December 1, 2007, at the Alamodome in San Antonio. The Sooners pulled away after a 14-14 halftime tie and ended Missouri's national title hopes.
summary: OU beat No. 1 Missouri 38-17 in the 2007 Big 12 Championship in San Antonio. It stood as the Sooners' last win over a No. 1 team until 2026.
body: Oklahoma has a long history of spoiling someone else's dream season, and the 2007 Big 12 Championship Game is one of the best examples. On December 1, 2007, at the Alamodome in San Antonio, the ninth-ranked Sooners beat No. 1 Missouri 38-17.

The game was tied 14-14 at halftime. After that it belonged to Oklahoma, which outscored Missouri 24-3 in the second half. Quarterback Sam Bradford completed 18 of 26 passes for 209 yards and two touchdowns, Chris Brown ran for two scores, and Allen Patrick added another. Linebacker Curtis Lofton came up with a key interception off a tipped pass that set up a Bradford touchdown.
OU's defense kept Missouri star Chase Daniel in check. He threw for 219 yards on 23-of-39 passing with no touchdown passes, scoring Missouri's only touchdown on a run.

The result had national ripple effects. Missouri's loss knocked it out of the BCS title game picture on a night when No. 2 West Virginia also lost. Oklahoma, which had already beaten Missouri in October, claimed its fifth Big 12 title since 2000 and a second straight trip to the Fiesta Bowl.

The win aged into an even better trivia answer. It stood as Oklahoma's most recent victory over a No. 1 team for nearly 19 years, until the Sooners upset No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry in October 2026.
